plan.title: Treated vs control liver DE with power and robustness checks
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is two-part: which genes differ between the 3 treated and 3 control human liver samples, and how much confidence 3 replicates per group buys. The data are 12000 genes x 6 samples of raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon (counts.csv) with a 6x2 metadata table (metadata.csv), unpaired, single batch. The plan follows the grounded procedure for this exact situation: (1) sample-structure QC with blind vst, PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a sample-distance heatmap to catch an outlier before any test, since with n=3 a single bad sample can dominate dispersion; (2) the primary DE call with DESeq2 Wald test, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples), median-of-ratios size factors, explicit control reference level, treated-vs-control contrast, apeglm LFC shrinkage for reporting, p-value histogram check, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; (3) an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered gene set as the second count model, because at 3 replicates the DESeq2/edgeR overlap is the accepted confidence measure — the intersection is the high-confidence gene set; (4) a report that leads with the power statement (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so power is computed from the closed form of sample size given depth and dispersion, stating the fold change detectable at 80% power), the per-method and intersection gene counts, MA and dispersion diagnostics, and the reproducibility record. Counts arrive already aggregated to gene level, so the tximport length-offset correction cannot be applied; this is stated as a limitation in the report. No pathway enrichment is planned — the research question does not ask for it.
